identity.description: Binance is a cryptocurrency exchange. Its API docs cover Spot, Margin, Convert, Wallet, USDS-M and COIN-M Futures, and the Agentic MCP server. The assigned binance-docs.github.io site redirects to developers.binance.com.
identity.identity_notes: Confirmed from the vendor docs redirect and the vendor GitHub org (github.com/binance, 'Open source, from Binance'). The binance-docs.github.io URL redirects to developers.binance.com, so the docs are the vendor's own. Not a generic 'Binance' app.

auth.scopes_notes: Agentic MCP server: 'Trade' and 'Transfer' require user confirmation; there is no withdrawal scope (see claims).

access.production_restrictions: Production (real-money) keys need a verified account and a Spot deposit before a key can be created, plus 2FA. Testnet credentials are self-serve after login. No paid plan or partner gate was found in the sources reviewed.

resources: USDS-M and COIN-M Futures (via Futures docs and Agentic MCP)
api.rate_limits: Limits are per IP, not per API key. Exceeding limits returns HTTP 429. Repeated violations lead to an IP ban (HTTP 418).
api.limitations: Webhooks not found; user data comes via WebSocket user data streams. The nav lists a FIX API, not verified. Futures/Margin endpoint details were not read; breadth is based on the Spot REST reference and the product nav. The Agentic MCP server is a limited, sub-account-only trade surface and has no withdrawals.

claims.value: Binance Spot API docs are the official vendor docs for Binance's exchange API; github.com/binance describes itself as 'Open source, from Binance'.
claims.quote: Official documentation for the Binance Spot APIs and streams.

claims.value: System-generated API keys use HMAC; self-generated keys use Ed25519 or RSA.
claims.quote: System-generated API keys use HMAC symmetric encryption.

claims.value: Secure endpoints accept HMAC, RSA, or Ed25519 keys; signed endpoints need a signature and timestamp.
claims.quote: We support HMAC, RSA, and Ed25519 keys.

claims.value: Testnet: log in on the testnet site and generate an API key; testnet balances are automatically granted.
claims.quote: Log in on this website, and generate an API Key.
All users registering on the Spot Test Network automatically receive a balance in many different assets.

claims.value: Before creating a key, a Spot deposit is required to activate the account; 2FA and identity verification are also needed.
claims.quote: you need to make a deposit of any amount to your Spot Account to activate your account.

claims.value: Limits are per IP, not per API key; violations get HTTP 429, and repeated violations lead to an IP ban.
claims.quote: The limits on the API are based on the IPs, not the API keys.

claims.value: Spot API offers WebSocket API and WebSocket Streams, including user data stream events over WebSocket.
claims.quote: You can now subscribe to User Data Stream events through your WebSocket API connection.

claims.value: Official connectors exist for Python, JS, Java, Go, Rust, and a Futures Python connector.
claims.quote: Simple Python connector to the Binance Futures API.
claims.verify_note: quote not found in fetched source text

claims.value: Binance's Agentic MCP server endpoint: https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic
claims.quote: Your agent trades inside a dedicated sub-account, isolated from your main account.

claims.value: Official MCP supports Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, ChatGPT, VS Code, and Grok.
claims.quote: Your agent can never move funds out of the sub-account to an external address.

claims.value: Multiple third-party community MCP servers for Binance exist (e.g., AnalyticAce, TermiX-official, ethancod1ng, py7hagoras, danishashko). These are not vendor-owned.

open_questions: The Agentic MCP server's auth method (OAuth vs API key vs other) is not named on the docs page. It only says 'Authenticate to authorize the connection.'
No public statement on whether the Agentic MCP server needs a paid plan, approval, or waitlist. Not found in the docs read.
Whether the FIX API (listed in the Spot docs nav) is publicly available was not verified.
Testnet pricing (free or paid) is not stated on the testnet page. Access appears to be self-serve, but this was not confirmed on a pricing page.
Regional and KYC restrictions (e.g., US or other jurisdictions) were not checked.
Webhook support was not found. Confirm whether Binance offers any webhook mechanism, or whether WebSocket user data streams are the only event channel.
Futures, Margin, Convert, and Wallet endpoint lists were not read; breadth rating is based on Spot REST and product nav.
Several community MCP servers exist, and their maintenance and safety were not vetted. Trust and ownership were not verified.

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented REST/WebSocket interface.
